options.text: Cooking can soften broccoli and reduce some nutrients such as vitamin C.
Cooking heat destroys all minerals in broccoli, so no nutrients remain.
Cooked broccoli contains no nutrients at all.
Loss of bright colour alone proves that every nutrient has been destroyed.

stem:
Nidhi compares raw broccoli with cooked broccoli. The cooked broccoli is softer and less bright green. A simple test shows that the cooked sample has less vitamin C than the raw sample.

Which claim correctly explains what cooking can do?

teacher.key_rationale: Cooking can change texture and colour and can reduce some nutrients such as vitamin C, but it does not wipe out all minerals or every nutrient, and colour loss alone does not prove total nutrient loss.
